# SE worker-storage cargo cap-ten native fixture

This is disposable test apparatus for one exact Factorio2.0.77, Space Exploration0.7.57, published4.7.20002 source-to-current candidate progression. It is not a migration admission, a reporter-save reconstruction, or a release result.

The fixture uses the same complete actor bytes for source, candidate, and both cold roles. Its data stage logs the sorted active-mod tuple and the seven typed `settings.startup[name].value` rows. It also logs the constructed worker technology without accepting the legacy five-pack construction: the candidate configuration callback must see and reject that real state before it queues any work.

`prerequisites.lua` is a reviewed literal 98-row prerequisite declaration rooted at `worker-robots-storage-3`, `se-space-science-lab`, and `se-material-science-pack-1`. Runtime only iterates the declaration for labelled fixture setup; it does not discover prerequisites, call recursive research, or treat those grants as cargo completions.

The [native prerequisite correction](../../../spec/evidence/se-cap-ten-prerequisite-literals-native-r01.json) adds the actual `se-heat-shielding` parent of `rocket-silo` and `se-fuel-refining` parent of `speed-module`; both parents already occur earlier in the same98-row declaration. The strict host world supplies these two native prototype rows independently of that declaration, so an omitted parent refuses before setup. The original2287 actor's source begin failure remains retained; the corrected declaration still requires a new native source run.

The [native setup callback correction](../../../spec/evidence/se-cap-ten-scripted-setup-native-r01.json) scopes completion observation to the source/candidate worker identities. The finite prerequisite setters can synchronously deliver their own completion events before a lab or worker frame exists; they remain labelled setup and are ignored by this worker observer. Scripted worker completions still refuse, including before source begin. The strict host setter now raises the corresponding callbacks. Console-interface errors are observed in the governed per-process stdout; the native file log can omit them and include multiple engine invocations.

The actor creates the actual electric `se-space-science-lab`, records its native researching speed10, and creates its bounded electric producer plus a Base `substation` at fixed non-overlapping positions. Before it feeds science, all three fixture-owned entities must report one non-nil electric network; the producer and lab must also report a connected native electric-network method result. The distributor is not required to satisfy that producer/consumer predicate. The actor never fills the lab buffer directly. It fills the real lab inventory with the seven captured science packs and temporarily records a documented force laboratory-speed stimulus. It records the pinned-API technology-price and laboratory-productivity context but does not change either. It never changes a lab prototype, target science unit, formula, time, effect, continuation level, progress, or bonus. Source events4–8 and candidate events9–10 must be engine events with `by_script=false`; each event must increase only the player worker-storage bonus by one while every other existing force remains unchanged. After ordinary source completion the fixture pauses and stages only the level-nine/tail queue on the next tick, rather than assuming an unbounded native queue. The product transfer must map source `worker-robots-storage-4` work to `mir-worker-storage-default-4` before candidate work; the actor records the raw canonical, private, and head rows separately from that logical paid frame. The level-eleven cap probe requires the naturally disabled private endpoint before it tries queue admission, then retains the unrelated tail current/queue and all seven science-unit observations unchanged. Each F200 science row is a normal-quality tool and records `count - 1 + durability / max_durability` through the pinned `LuaItemStack`/`LuaItemCommon` and `LuaItemPrototype.get_durability` APIs, so the saved frames retain fractional tool loss. The host `.42` partial is only a synthetic reader exercise: native evidence must supply actual tool-unit observations and independently justify any cost/rounding conclusion. `on_load` only records the persisted phase in local state. On the first tick, a persisted source `idle` state may still be `idle` or have become `source-working` through the source command, while a persisted `source-partial` state must have become `candidate-working` through configuration. Another persisted pre-closed phase refuses. A persisted closed endpoint is separately read without feeding, saving, granting research, or initializing persistent state.
